newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close down 3.6 pct on poll jitters.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close down 3.6 pct on poll jitters.

text.p: French stocks slumped on Wednesday on talk that privately-commissioned polls showed the opposition Socialists well placed going into the parliamentary election runoff on Sunday, brokers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 97.17 points, or 3.63 percent, to 2,583.17. The CAC-40 May futures contract fell 88 points to 2,590.
It was the second selloff on the bourse this week as investors priced in the risk that the Socialists, who won the first round last Sunday, could win on June 1, dealers said.
The CAC index lost 3.91 percent on Monday, then rebounded nearly one percent on Tuesday before poll rumours triggered fresh selling on Wednesday in very heavy turnover of 12.45 billion francs.

"We are seeing a follow-through from Monday. There has been a lot of complacency in the market and people did not take fully into account that the right could lose," said Merrill Lynch market strategist David Bowers.

Equities are seen as vulnerable because while the Socialists would not be expected to scupper plans to join a single European currency, they might block or delay structural reforms and sector restructurings proposed by the centre-right RPR-UDF coalition.

Shares in sectors due for restructurings were hit hardest. In the financial sector, BNP's stock tumbled 7.13 percent to 233 francs, Societe Generale shares fell 6.27 percent to 613 francs, and Compagnie Bancaire fell 5.87 percent to 657 francs.
The car sector was also weak, with Renault's stock falling 7.89 percent to 133.10 francs and tyremaker Michelin's stock losing 4.44 percent to 325 francs.

Privatisation stocks were hammered on concerns a Socialist-led government might block or delay privatisations. Shares in defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF fell 4.57 percent, while stock in bidders Lagardere and Alcatel Alsthom fell 4.61 percent and 5.26 percent, respectively.
Shares in Dassault Aviation, which is being merged with soon-to-be-privatised Aerospatiale, lost another 7.79 percent to 1,077 francs on fears Aerospatiale might not be privatised.
Investors sought haven in stocks in building and public works firms. Shares in Bouygues fell 1.18 percent, while shares in its 59 percent owned unit Colas rose 5.98 percent.

Luxury goods group LVMH's stock also outperformed, closing down 1.63 percent at 1,389, after LVMH said it would exercise options to buy back Guinness Plc's stakes in Moet Hennessy and the joint distribution ventures between the two companies.

The move is seen as a way to put pressure on Guinness and its merger partner Grand Met. Analysts say LVMH's objective is to be the biggest shareholder in a group merging the Guinness-Grand Met drinks businesses with those of LVMH's Moet Hennessy unit.
